name: Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣūlī
summary: Man of letters and boon companion of the ʿAbbāsid caliphs, who gathered the poems of the caliphs and of the poets and wrote Adab al-kuttāb and al-Awrāq.
bio: Ibn al-Anbārī calls al-Ṣūlī learned in the branches of letters, acquainted with the manners of kings and caliphs and skilled in writing books: the boon companion of several caliphs, he collected their poems and those of many poets.
He died in Basra in 335/946, in hiding (some say 336).

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 343–345
